preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership)
Attacker must hold some KARMA tokens to initiate transfers

violation_target.exploit_hint: The vulnerability is in the _takeLiquidity function where burnAmount is subtracted from _tTotalSupply but not from _tTotal. As owner, set burn fees to a high percentage (e.g., 100), then perform a transfer to trigger the burn mechanism. This will reduce totalSupply() while keeping _tTotal unchanged, creating an imbalance where sum(balances) > totalSupply(). Then swap tokens for ETH at the inflated valuation before the discrepancy is corrected.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has two total supply variables: _tTotal (fixed) and _tTotalSupply (decreases on burns). When tokens are burned via _takeLiquidity(), _tTotalSupply decreases but _tTotal remains unchanged. This increases the reflection rate (rSupply/tSupply), making reflected balances worth more tokens than they should be. An attacker can trigger burns to artificially inflate their token balance.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Acquire initial tokens by buying from the pair. 2. Trigger the burn mechanism by causing a swap that collects fees and calls _takeLiquidity. 3. The burn reduces _tTotalSupply, increasing the reflection rate. 4. Our reflected balance is now worth more tokens. 5. Transfer tokens to realize the profit.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Start with some BNB to buy tokens. 2. Buy tokens from the pair (this will pay fees that accumulate in the contract). 3. Trigger the swap mechanism by selling tokens back to the pair, which will cause the contract to swap accumulated fees for BNB and add liquidity (including burning). 4. After the burn, our reflected balance is worth more tokens. 5. Transfer tokens to another address to realize the increased value.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has two total supply variables: _tTotal (fixed) and _tTotalSupply (decreases on burns). When tokens are burned via _takeLiquidity(), _tTotalSupply decreases but _tTotal remains unchanged. This increases the reflection rate (rSupply/tSupply), making reflected balances worth more tokens than they should be. The key is to trigger the burn mechanism by accumulating enough fees in the contract to reach swapTokensAtAmount, then trigger a swap to the pair.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Buy tokens to accumulate fees in the contract. 2. Sell tokens to trigger the contract's swap mechanism when contract balance >= swapTokensAtAmount. 3. The swap will call _takeLiquidity which burns tokens, reducing _tTotalSupply. 4. This increases the reflection rate, making our reflected balance worth more tokens. 5. Transfer tokens to realize the profit.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Remove the enableTrading() call since trading is already enabled. 2. Buy tokens to pay fees that accumulate in the contract. 3. Check contract balance and swap threshold. 4. If needed, make more trades to accumulate enough fees. 5. Trigger the swap mechanism by selling to the pair. 6. After burns occur, check our increased balance.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because trading was already enabled on the contract, so the enableTrading() call reverted. We don't need to enable trading since it's already active.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has two total supply variables: _tTotal (fixed) and _tTotalSupply (decreases on burns). When tokens are burned via _takeLiquidity(), _tTotalSupply decreases but _tTotal remains unchanged. This increases the reflection rate (rSupply/tSupply), making reflected balances worth more tokens. We need to trigger burns while respecting transaction limits.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Buy tokens in amounts below maxTransactionAmountBuy. 2. Sell tokens in amounts below maxTransactionAmountSell to accumulate fees. 3. Repeat small trades until contract has enough fees to trigger swap. 4. Trigger swap mechanism which will burn tokens. 5. After burns, our reflected balance is worth more tokens.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Calculate max transaction amounts. 2. Buy tokens with amount below maxTransactionAmountBuy. 3. Sell tokens with amount below maxTransactionAmountSell to pay fees. 4. Check contract balance vs swap threshold. 5. Repeat small trades if needed. 6. Trigger final swap to cause burns. 7. Verify balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because it violated the max transaction amount limits (anti-whale). The contract has maxTransactionAmountBuy and maxTransactionAmountSell set to 1.5% of total supply. We need to ensure our trade amounts stay below these limits.
